title: Premium Billing Accounts Terms: Grace Period, Cure and Lapse
content:
**Entering grace.** An active Premium Billing Accounts arrangement enters grace period on the day after a premium due date on which the coverage month due is not fully paid; its grace-period start date is the first day of that unpaid month.

**Length of the grace period.**
- For a non-APTC account the grace period lasts the arrangement's grace period in calendar days, counted from the due date of the first unpaid month.
- For an exchange account that receives advance premium tax credit and has paid its binder, it lasts the arrangement's APTC grace in consecutive calendar months, starting with the first unpaid month.

**During grace.** Coverage continues. On an APTC account, claims with dates of service from the arrangement's claims-pended grace month onward are pended; on other accounts claims are paid normally.

**Cure.** The grace period is cured when every past-due month is fully paid before it ends, and the account returns to active.

**When lapse is allowed.** An account in grace may lapse only after its grace period has ended without full payment of the past-due premium. The grace period ends at the close of the due date of the first unpaid month plus the grace period in calendar days (for APTC accounts, the last day of the last grace month), and lapse is allowed only on a later day. The judgement rests on the account's recorded grace-period start date as the company's system shows it before the lapse is booked, not on what the customer states.

**On lapse.** Every enrollment the account funds terminates for nonpayment. The termination date is the paid-through date or, on an APTC account, the last day of the first grace month; the advance premium tax credit received for the later grace months is returned to the exchange. A partial payment that leaves any past-due month short of the payment threshold does not stop the lapse.

**Worked dates (hypothetical; 31-day grace).** The first unpaid month begins on 1 June, so the grace-period start date is 1 June. 1 June plus 31 calendar days is 2 July; the grace period ends at the close of 2 July.
| Day considered | Lapse allowed? |
|---|---|
| 2 July (the end day itself) | no — the grace period has not yet ended |
| 3 July (the next day) | yes, if the past-due premium is still not fully paid |

**Worked dates (hypothetical APTC account with a 3-month grace).** The first unpaid month is June: the grace months are June, July and August, the grace period ends on 31 August and lapse is allowed from 1 September. On lapse the termination date is 30 June, the last day of the first grace month, and claims with dates of service from July, the second grace month, onward were pended.
